- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

attachment.content:
- graphify: Use for any question about a codebase, its architecture, file relationships, or project content — especially when graphify-out/ exists, where the question should be treated as a graphify query first. Turns any input (code, docs, papers, images, videos) into a persistent knowledge graph with god nodes, community detection, and query/path/explain tools.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

21	// Migration System Overview:
22	//
23	// The migration system handles database schema versioning and upgrades.
24	// Schema version is stored in system_setting.
25	//
26	// Migration Flow:
27	// 1. preMigrate: Check if DB is initialized. If not, apply LATEST.sql
28	// 2. checkMinimumUpgradeVersion: Verify installation can be upgraded (reject pre-0.22 installations)
29	// 3. Migrate (prod mode): Apply incremental migrations from current to target version
30	// 4. Migrate (demo mode): Seed database with demo data
31	// Deployment configuration is loaded separately after migration completes.
32	//
33	// Version Tracking:
34	// - New installations: Schema version set in system_setting immediately
35	// - Existing v0.22+ installations: Schema version tracked in system_setting
36	// - Pre-v0.22 installations: Must upgrade to v0.25.x first (migration_history → system_setting migration)
37	//
38	// Migration Files:
39	// - Location: store/migration/{driver}/{version}/NN__description.sql
40	// - Naming: NN is zero-padded patch number, description is human-readable
41	// - Ordering: Files sorted lexicographically and applied in order
42	// - LATEST.sql: Full schema for new installations (faster than incremental migrations)
43	
44	//go:embed migration
45	var migrationFS embed.FS
46	
47	//go:embed seed
48	var seedFS embed.FS
49	
50	const (
51		// MigrateFileNameSplit is the split character between the patch version and the description in the migration file name.
52		// For example, "1__create_table.sql".
53		MigrateFileNameSplit = "__"
54		// LatestSchemaFileName is the name of the latest schema file.
55		// This file is used to initialize fresh installations with the current schema.
56		LatestSchemaFileName = "LATEST.sql"
57	
58		// defaultSchemaVersion is used when schema version is empty or not set.
59		// This handles edge cases for old installations without version tracking.
60		defaultSchemaVersion = "0.0.0"
61	)

63	// getSchemaVersionOrDefault returns the schema version or default if empty.
64	// This ensures safe version comparisons and handles old installations.
65	func getSchemaVersionOrDefault(schemaVersion string) string {
66		if schemaVersion == "" {
67			return defaultSchemaVersion
68		}
69		return schemaVersion
70	}
71	
72	// isVersionEmpty checks if the schema version is empty or the default value.
73	func isVersionEmpty(schemaVersion string) bool {
74		return schemaVersion == "" || schemaVersion == defaultSchemaVersion
75	}
76	
77	// shouldApplyMigration determines if a migration file should be applied.
78	// It checks if the file's version is between the current DB version and target version.
79	func shouldApplyMigration(fileVersion, currentDBVersion, targetVersion string) bool {
80		currentDBVersionSafe := getSchemaVersionOrDefault(currentDBVersion)
81		return version.IsVersionGreaterThan(fileVersion, currentDBVersionSafe) &&
82			version.IsVersionGreaterOrEqualThan(targetVersion, fileVersion)
83	}
84	
85	// validateMigrationFileName checks if a migration file follows the expected naming convention.
86	// Expected format: "NN__description.sql" where NN is a zero-padded number.
87	func validateMigrationFileName(filename string) error {
88		parts := strings.SplitN(filename, MigrateFileNameSplit, 2)
89		if len(parts) < 2 {
90			return errors.Errorf("invalid migration filename format (missing %s): %s", MigrateFileNameSplit, filename)
91		}
92		if _, err := strconv.Atoi(parts[0]); err != nil {
93			return errors.Errorf("migration filename must start with a number: %s", filename)
94		}
95		return nil
96	}

98	// Migrate migrates the database schema to the latest version.
99	// It checks the current schema version and applies any necessary migrations.
100	// It also seeds the database with initial data if in demo mode.
101	func (s *Store) Migrate(ctx context.Context) error {
102		if err := s.preMigrate(ctx); err != nil {
103			return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to pre-migrate")
104		}
105	
106		instanceBasicSetting, err := s.GetInstanceBasicSetting(ctx)
107		if err != nil {
108			return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to get instance basic setting")
109		}
110		currentSchemaVersion, err := s.GetCurrentSchemaVersion()
111		if err != nil {
112			return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to get current schema version")
113		}
114		// Check for downgrade (but skip if schema version is empty - that means fresh/old installation)
115		if !isVersionEmpty(instanceBasicSetting.SchemaVersion) && version.IsVersionGreaterThan(instanceBasicSetting.SchemaVersion, currentSchemaVersion) {
116			slog.Error("cannot downgrade schema version",
117				slog.String("databaseVersion", instanceBasicSetting.SchemaVersion),
118				slog.String("currentVersion", currentSchemaVersion),
119			)
120			return errors.Errorf("cannot downgrade schema version from %s to %s", instanceBasicSetting.SchemaVersion, currentSchemaVersion)
121		}
122		// Apply migrations if needed.
123		if isVersionEmpty(instanceBasicSetting.SchemaVersion) || version.IsVersionGreaterThan(currentSchemaVersion, instanceBasicSetting.SchemaVersion) {
124			if err := s.applyMigrations(ctx, instanceBasicSetting.SchemaVersion, currentSchemaVersion); err != nil {
125				return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to apply migrations")
126			}
127		}
128	
129		if s.profile.Demo {
130			// In demo mode, we should seed the database.
131			if err := s.seed(ctx); err != nil {
132				return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to seed")
133			}
134		}
135		return nil
136	}

138	// applyMigrations applies all necessary migration files between current and target schema versions.
139	// It runs all migrations in a single transaction for atomicity.
140	func (s *Store) applyMigrations(ctx context.Context, currentSchemaVersion, targetSchemaVersion string) error {
141		filePaths, err := fs.Glob(migrationFS, fmt.Sprintf("%s*/*.sql", s.getMigrationBasePath()))
142		if err != nil {
143			return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to read migration files")
144		}
145		slices.Sort(filePaths)
146	
147		// Start a transaction to apply migrations atomically
148		tx, err := s.driver.GetDB().Begin()
149		if err != nil {
150			return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to start transaction")
151		}
152		defer tx.Rollback()
153	
154		// Use safe version for comparison (handles empty version case)
155		schemaVersionForComparison := getSchemaVersionOrDefault(currentSchemaVersion)
156		if isVersionEmpty(currentSchemaVersion) {
157			slog.Warn("schema version is empty, treating as default for migration comparison",
158				slog.String("defaultVersion", defaultSchemaVersion))
159		}
160	
161		slog.Info("start migration",
162			slog.String("currentSchemaVersion", schemaVersionForComparison),
163			slog.String("targetSchemaVersion", targetSchemaVersion))
164	
165		migrationsApplied := 0
166		for _, filePath := range filePaths {
167			fileSchemaVersion, err := s.getSchemaVersionOfMigrateScript(filePath)
168			if err != nil {
169				return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to get schema version of migrate script")
170			}
171	
172			if shouldApplyMigration(fileSchemaVersion, currentSchemaVersion, targetSchemaVersion) {
173				// Validate migration filename before applying
174				filename := filepath.Base(filePath)
175				if err := validateMigrationFileName(filename); err != nil {
176					slog.Warn("migration file has invalid name but will be applied", slog.String("file", filePath), slog.String("error", err.Error()))
177				}
178	
179				slog.Info("applying migration",
180					slog.String("file", filePath),
181					slog.String("version", fileSchemaVersion))
182	
183				bytes, err := migrationFS.ReadFile(filePath)
184				if err != nil {
185					return errors.Wrapf(err, "failed to read migration file: %s", filePath)
186				}
187	
188				stmt := string(bytes)
189				if err := s.execute(ctx, tx, stmt); err != nil {
190					return errors.Wrapf(err, "failed to execute migration %s: %s", filePath, err)
191				}
192				migrationsApplied++
193			}
194		}
195	
196		if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
197			return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to commit migration transaction")
198		}
199	
200		slog.Info("migration completed", slog.Int("migrationsApplied", migrationsApplied))
201	
202		// Update schema version after successful migration
203		if err := s.updateCurrentSchemaVersion(ctx, targetSchemaVersion); err != nil {
204			return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to update current schema version")
205		}
206	
207		return nil
208	}

210	// preMigrate checks if the database is initialized and applies the latest schema if not.
211	func (s *Store) preMigrate(ctx context.Context) error {
212		initialized, err := s.driver.IsInitialized(ctx)
213		if err != nil {
214			return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to check if database is initialized")
215		}
216	
217		if !initialized {
218			filePath := s.getMigrationBasePath() + LatestSchemaFileName
219			bytes, err := migrationFS.ReadFile(filePath)
220			if err != nil {
221				return errors.Errorf("failed to read latest schema file: %s", err)
222			}
223			// Start a transaction to apply the latest schema.
224			tx, err := s.driver.GetDB().Begin()
225			if err != nil {
226				return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to start transaction")
227			}
228			defer tx.Rollback()
229			slog.Info("initializing new database with latest schema", slog.String("file", filePath))
230			if err := s.execute(ctx, tx, string(bytes)); err != nil {
231				return errors.Errorf("failed to execute SQL file %s, err %s", filePath, err)
232			}
233			if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
234				return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to commit transaction")
235			}
236	
237			// Upsert current schema version to database.
238			schemaVersion, err := s.GetCurrentSchemaVersion()
239			if err != nil {
240				return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to get current schema version")
241			}
242			slog.Info("database initialized successfully", slog.String("schemaVersion", schemaVersion))
243			if err := s.updateCurrentSchemaVersion(ctx, schemaVersion); err != nil {
244				return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to update current schema version")
245			}
246		}
247	
248		if err := s.checkMinimumUpgradeVersion(ctx); err != nil {
249			return err // Error message is already descriptive, don't wrap it
250		}
251		return nil
252	}

262	// seed seeds the database with initial data.
263	// It reads all seed files from the embedded filesystem and executes them in order.
264	// This is only supported for SQLite databases and is used in demo mode.
265	func (s *Store) seed(ctx context.Context) error {
266		// Only seed for SQLite - other databases should use production data
267		if s.profile.Driver != "sqlite" {
268			slog.Warn("seed is only supported for SQLite, skipping for other databases")
269			return nil
270		}
271	
272		filenames, err := fs.Glob(seedFS, fmt.Sprintf("%s*.sql", s.getSeedBasePath()))
273		if err != nil {
274			return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to read seed files")
275		}
276	
277		// Sort seed files by name. This is important to ensure that seed files are applied in order.
278		slices.Sort(filenames)
279		// Start a transaction to apply the seed files.
280		tx, err := s.driver.GetDB().Begin()
281		if err != nil {
282			return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to start transaction")
283		}
284		defer tx.Rollback()
285		// Loop over all seed files and execute them in order.
286		for _, filename := range filenames {
287			bytes, err := seedFS.ReadFile(filename)
288			if err != nil {
289				return errors.Wrapf(err, "failed to read seed file, filename=%s", filename)
290			}
291			if err := s.execute(ctx, tx, string(bytes)); err != nil {
292				return errors.Wrapf(err, "seed error: %s", filename)
293			}
294		}
295		return tx.Commit()
296	}

298	// GetCurrentSchemaVersion returns the latest schema version available for the configured database driver.
299	func (s *Store) GetCurrentSchemaVersion() (string, error) {
300		filePaths, err := fs.Glob(migrationFS, fmt.Sprintf("%s*/*.sql", s.getMigrationBasePath()))
301		if err != nil {
302			return "", errors.Wrap(err, "failed to read migration files")
303		}
304		if len(filePaths) == 0 {
305			return defaultSchemaVersion, nil
306		}
307	
308		currentSchemaVersion := defaultSchemaVersion
309		for _, filePath := range filePaths {
310			fileSchemaVersion, err := s.getSchemaVersionOfMigrateScript(filePath)
311			if err != nil {
312				return "", errors.Wrap(err, "failed to get schema version of migrate script")
313			}
314			if version.IsVersionGreaterThan(fileSchemaVersion, currentSchemaVersion) {
315				currentSchemaVersion = fileSchemaVersion
316			}
317		}
318		return currentSchemaVersion, nil
319	}

321	// getSchemaVersionOfMigrateScript extracts the schema version from the migration script file path.
322	// It returns the schema version in the format "major.minor.patch".
323	// If the file is the latest schema file, it returns the current schema version.
324	func (s *Store) getSchemaVersionOfMigrateScript(filePath string) (string, error) {
325		// If the file is the latest schema file, return the current schema version.
326		if strings.HasSuffix(filePath, LatestSchemaFileName) {
327			return s.GetCurrentSchemaVersion()
328		}
329	
330		normalizedPath := filepath.ToSlash(filePath)
331		elements := strings.Split(normalizedPath, "/")
332		if len(elements) < 2 {
333			return "", errors.Errorf("invalid file path: %s", filePath)
334		}
335		minorVersion := elements[len(elements)-2]
336		rawPatchVersion := strings.Split(elements[len(elements)-1], MigrateFileNameSplit)[0]
337		patchVersion, err := strconv.Atoi(rawPatchVersion)
338		if err != nil {
339			return "", errors.Wrapf(err, "failed to convert patch version to int: %s", rawPatchVersion)
340		}
341		return fmt.Sprintf("%s.%d", minorVersion, patchVersion+1), nil
342	}

353	// updateCurrentSchemaVersion updates the current schema version in the instance basic setting.
354	// It retrieves the instance basic setting, updates the schema version, and upserts the setting back to the database.
355	func (s *Store) updateCurrentSchemaVersion(ctx context.Context, schemaVersion string) error {
356		instanceBasicSetting, err := s.GetInstanceBasicSetting(ctx)
357		if err != nil {
358			return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to get instance basic setting")
359		}
360		instanceBasicSetting.SchemaVersion = schemaVersion
361		if _, err := s.UpsertInstanceSetting(ctx, &storepb.InstanceSetting{
362			Key:   storepb.InstanceSettingKey_BASIC,
363			Value: &storepb.InstanceSetting_BasicSetting{BasicSetting: instanceBasicSetting},
364		}); err != nil {
365			return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to upsert instance setting")
366		}
367		return nil
368	}

370	// checkMinimumUpgradeVersion verifies the installation meets minimum version requirements for upgrade.
371	// For very old installations (< v0.22.0), users must upgrade to v0.25.x first before upgrading to current version.
372	// This is necessary because schema version tracking was moved from migration_history to system_setting in v0.22.0.
373	func (s *Store) checkMinimumUpgradeVersion(ctx context.Context) error {
374		instanceBasicSetting, err := s.GetInstanceBasicSetting(ctx)
375		if err != nil {
376			return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to get instance basic setting")
377		}
378		schemaVersion := instanceBasicSetting.SchemaVersion
379	
380		// Modern installation: nothing to check.
381		if !isVersionEmpty(schemaVersion) && version.IsVersionGreaterOrEqualThan(schemaVersion, "0.22.0") {
382			return nil
383		}
384	
385		// Schema version is empty for fresh installs too, but preMigrate sets it before we get here.
386		// So empty schema version on an initialized DB means a pre-v0.22 legacy installation.
387		if isVersionEmpty(schemaVersion) {
388			initialized, err := s.driver.IsInitialized(ctx)
389			if err != nil {
390				return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to check if database is initialized")
391			}
392			if !initialized {
393				return nil
394			}
395		}
396	
397		// schemaVersion is either set but < 0.22.0, or empty on an initialized (legacy) DB.
398		currentVersion, _ := s.GetCurrentSchemaVersion()
399		return errors.Errorf(
400			"Your Memos installation is too old to upgrade directly.\n\n"+
401				"Your current version: %s\n"+
402				"Target version: %s\n"+
403				"Minimum required: v0.22.0 (May 2024)\n\n"+
404				"Upgrade path:\n"+
405				"1. First upgrade to v0.25.3: https://github.com/usememos/memos/releases/tag/v0.25.3\n"+
406				"2. Start the server and verify it works\n"+
407				"3. Then upgrade to the latest version\n\n"+
408				"This is required because schema version tracking was moved from migration_history\n"+
409				"to system_setting in v0.22.0. The intermediate upgrade handles this migration safely.",
410			schemaVersion,
411			currentVersion,
412		)

21	// Migration System Overview:
22	//
23	// The migration system handles database schema versioning and upgrades.
24	// Schema version is stored in system_setting.
25	//
26	// Migration Flow:
27	// 1. preMigrate: Check if DB is initialized. If not, apply LATEST.sql
28	// 2. checkMinimumUpgradeVersion: Verify installation can be upgraded (reject pre-0.22 installations)
29	// 3. Migrate (prod mode): Apply incremental migrations from current to target version
30	// 4. Migrate (demo mode): Seed database with demo data
31	// Deployment configuration is loaded separately after migration completes.
32	//
33	// Version Tracking:
34	// - New installations: Schema version set in system_setting immediately
35	// - Existing v0.22+ installations: Schema version tracked in system_setting
36	// - Pre-v0.22 installations: Must upgrade to v0.25.x first (migration_history → system_setting migration)
37	//
38	// Migration Files:
39	// - Location: store/migration/{driver}/{version}/NN__description.sql
40	// - Naming: NN is zero-padded patch number, description is human-readable
41	// - Ordering: Files sorted lexicographically and applied in order
42	// - LATEST.sql: Full schema for new installations (faster than incremental migrations)
43	
44	//go:embed migration
45	var migrationFS embed.FS
46	
47	//go:embed seed
48	var seedFS embed.FS
49	
50	const (
51		// MigrateFileNameSplit is the split character between the patch version and the description in the migration file name.
52		// For example, "1__create_table.sql".
53		MigrateFileNameSplit = "__"
54		// LatestSchemaFileName is the name of the latest schema file.
55		// This file is used to initialize fresh installations with the current schema.
56		LatestSchemaFileName = "LATEST.sql"
57	
58		// defaultSchemaVersion is used when schema version is empty or not set.
59		// This handles edge cases for old installations without version tracking.
60		defaultSchemaVersion = "0.0.0"
61	)

63	// getSchemaVersionOrDefault returns the schema version or default if empty.
64	// This ensures safe version comparisons and handles old installations.
65	func getSchemaVersionOrDefault(schemaVersion string) string {
66		if schemaVersion == "" {
67			return defaultSchemaVersion
68		}
69		return schemaVersion
70	}
71	
72	// isVersionEmpty checks if the schema version is empty or the default value.
73	func isVersionEmpty(schemaVersion string) bool {
74		return schemaVersion == "" || schemaVersion == defaultSchemaVersion
75	}
76	
77	// shouldApplyMigration determines if a migration file should be applied.
78	// It checks if the file's version is between the current DB version and target version.
79	func shouldApplyMigration(fileVersion, currentDBVersion, targetVersion string) bool {
80		currentDBVersionSafe := getSchemaVersionOrDefault(currentDBVersion)
81		return version.IsVersionGreaterThan(fileVersion, currentDBVersionSafe) &&
82			version.IsVersionGreaterOrEqualThan(targetVersion, fileVersion)
83	}
84	
85	// validateMigrationFileName checks if a migration file follows the expected naming convention.
86	// Expected format: "NN__description.sql" where NN is a zero-padded number.
87	func validateMigrationFileName(filename string) error {
88		parts := strings.SplitN(filename, MigrateFileNameSplit, 2)
89		if len(parts) < 2 {
90			return errors.Errorf("invalid migration filename format (missing %s): %s", MigrateFileNameSplit, filename)
91		}
92		if _, err := strconv.Atoi(parts[0]); err != nil {
93			return errors.Errorf("migration filename must start with a number: %s", filename)
94		}
95		return nil
96	}

98	// Migrate migrates the database schema to the latest version.
99	// It checks the current schema version and applies any necessary migrations.
100	// It also seeds the database with initial data if in demo mode.
101	func (s *Store) Migrate(ctx context.Context) error {
102		if err := s.preMigrate(ctx); err != nil {
103			return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to pre-migrate")
104		}
105	
106		instanceBasicSetting, err := s.GetInstanceBasicSetting(ctx)
107		if err != nil {
108			return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to get instance basic setting")
109		}
110		currentSchemaVersion, err := s.GetCurrentSchemaVersion()
111		if err != nil {
112			return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to get current schema version")
113		}
114		// Check for downgrade (but skip if schema version is empty - that means fresh/old installation)
115		if !isVersionEmpty(instanceBasicSetting.SchemaVersion) && version.IsVersionGreaterThan(instanceBasicSetting.SchemaVersion, currentSchemaVersion) {
116			slog.Error("cannot downgrade schema version",
117				slog.String("databaseVersion", instanceBasicSetting.SchemaVersion),
118				slog.String("currentVersion", currentSchemaVersion),
119			)
120			return errors.Errorf("cannot downgrade schema version from %s to %s", instanceBasicSetting.SchemaVersion, currentSchemaVersion)
121		}
122		// Apply migrations if needed.
123		if isVersionEmpty(instanceBasicSetting.SchemaVersion) || version.IsVersionGreaterThan(currentSchemaVersion, instanceBasicSetting.SchemaVersion) {
124			if err := s.applyMigrations(ctx, instanceBasicSetting.SchemaVersion, currentSchemaVersion); err != nil {
125				return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to apply migrations")
126			}
127		}
128	
129		if s.profile.Demo {
130			// In demo mode, we should seed the database.
131			if err := s.seed(ctx); err != nil {
132				return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to seed")
133			}
134		}
135		return nil
136	}

138	// applyMigrations applies all necessary migration files between current and target schema versions.
139	// It runs all migrations in a single transaction for atomicity.
140	func (s *Store) applyMigrations(ctx context.Context, currentSchemaVersion, targetSchemaVersion string) error {
141		filePaths, err := fs.Glob(migrationFS, fmt.Sprintf("%s*/*.sql", s.getMigrationBasePath()))
142		if err != nil {
143			return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to read migration files")
144		}
145		slices.Sort(filePaths)
146	
147		// Start a transaction to apply migrations atomically
148		tx, err := s.driver.GetDB().Begin()
149		if err != nil {
150			return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to start transaction")
151		}
152		defer tx.Rollback()
153	
154		// Use safe version for comparison (handles empty version case)
155		schemaVersionForComparison := getSchemaVersionOrDefault(currentSchemaVersion)
156		if isVersionEmpty(currentSchemaVersion) {
157			slog.Warn("schema version is empty, treating as default for migration comparison",
158				slog.String("defaultVersion", defaultSchemaVersion))
159		}
160	
161		slog.Info("start migration",
162			slog.String("currentSchemaVersion", schemaVersionForComparison),
163			slog.String("targetSchemaVersion", targetSchemaVersion))
164	
165		migrationsApplied := 0
166		for _, filePath := range filePaths {
167			fileSchemaVersion, err := s.getSchemaVersionOfMigrateScript(filePath)
168			if err != nil {
169				return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to get schema version of migrate script")
170			}
171	
172			if shouldApplyMigration(fileSchemaVersion, currentSchemaVersion, targetSchemaVersion) {
173				// Validate migration filename before applying
174				filename := filepath.Base(filePath)
175				if err := validateMigrationFileName(filename); err != nil {
176					slog.Warn("migration file has invalid name but will be applied", slog.String("file", filePath), slog.String("error", err.Error()))
177				}
178	
179				slog.Info("applying migration",
180					slog.String("file", filePath),
181					slog.String("version", fileSchemaVersion))
182	
183				bytes, err := migrationFS.ReadFile(filePath)
184				if err != nil {
185					return errors.Wrapf(err, "failed to read migration file: %s", filePath)
186				}
187	
188				stmt := string(bytes)
189				if err := s.execute(ctx, tx, stmt); err != nil {
190					return errors.Wrapf(err, "failed to execute migration %s: %s", filePath, err)
191				}
192				migrationsApplied++
193			}
194		}
195	
196		if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
197			return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to commit migration transaction")
198		}
199	
200		slog.Info("migration completed", slog.Int("migrationsApplied", migrationsApplied))
201	
202		// Update schema version after successful migration
203		if err := s.updateCurrentSchemaVersion(ctx, targetSchemaVersion); err != nil {
204			return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to update current schema version")
205		}
206	
207		return nil
208	}

210	// preMigrate checks if the database is initialized and applies the latest schema if not.
211	func (s *Store) preMigrate(ctx context.Context) error {
212		initialized, err := s.driver.IsInitialized(ctx)
213		if err != nil {
214			return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to check if database is initialized")
215		}
216	
217		if !initialized {
218			filePath := s.getMigrationBasePath() + LatestSchemaFileName
219			bytes, err := migrationFS.ReadFile(filePath)
220			if err != nil {
221				return errors.Errorf("failed to read latest schema file: %s", err)
222			}
223			// Start a transaction to apply the latest schema.
224			tx, err := s.driver.GetDB().Begin()
225			if err != nil {
226				return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to start transaction")
227			}
228			defer tx.Rollback()
229			slog.Info("initializing new database with latest schema", slog.String("file", filePath))
230			if err := s.execute(ctx, tx, string(bytes)); err != nil {
231				return errors.Errorf("failed to execute SQL file %s, err %s", filePath, err)
232			}
233			if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
234				return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to commit transaction")
235			}
236	
237			// Upsert current schema version to database.
238			schemaVersion, err := s.GetCurrentSchemaVersion()
239			if err != nil {

262	// seed seeds the database with initial data.
263	// It reads all seed files from the embedded filesystem and executes them in order.
264	// This is only supported for SQLite databases and is used in demo mode.
265	func (s *Store) seed(ctx context.Context) error {
266		// Only seed for SQLite - other databases should use production data
267		if s.profile.Driver != "sqlite" {
268			slog.Warn("seed is only supported for SQLite, skipping for other databases")
269			return nil
270		}
271	
272		filenames, err := fs.Glob(seedFS, fmt.Sprintf("%s*.sql", s.getSeedBasePath()))
273		if err != nil {
274			return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to read seed files")
275		}
276	
277		// Sort seed files by name. This is important to ensure that seed files are applied in order.
278		slices.Sort(filenames)
279		// Start a transaction to apply the seed files.
280		tx, err := s.driver.GetDB().Begin()
281		if err != nil {
282			return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to start transaction")
283		}
284		defer tx.Rollback()
285		// Loop over all seed files and execute them in order.
286		for _, filename := range filenames {
287			bytes, err := seedFS.ReadFile(filename)
288			if err != nil {
289				return errors.Wrapf(err, "failed to read seed file, filename=%s", filename)
290			}
291			if err := s.execute(ctx, tx, string(bytes)); err != nil {
292				return errors.Wrapf(err, "seed error: %s", filename)
293			}
294		}
295		return tx.Commit()
296	}

298	// GetCurrentSchemaVersion returns the latest schema version available for the configured database driver.
299	func (s *Store) GetCurrentSchemaVersion() (string, error) {
300		filePaths, err := fs.Glob(migrationFS, fmt.Sprintf("%s*/*.sql", s.getMigrationBasePath()))
301		if err != nil {
302			return "", errors.Wrap(err, "failed to read migration files")
303		}
304		if len(filePaths) == 0 {
305			return defaultSchemaVersion, nil
306		}
307	
308		currentSchemaVersion := defaultSchemaVersion
309		for _, filePath := range filePaths {
310			fileSchemaVersion, err := s.getSchemaVersionOfMigrateScript(filePath)
311			if err != nil {
312				return "", errors.Wrap(err, "failed to get schema version of migrate script")
313			}
314			if version.IsVersionGreaterThan(fileSchemaVersion, currentSchemaVersion) {
315				currentSchemaVersion = fileSchemaVersion
316			}
317		}
318		return currentSchemaVersion, nil
319	}

321	// getSchemaVersionOfMigrateScript extracts the schema version from the migration script file path.
322	// It returns the schema version in the format "major.minor.patch".
323	// If the file is the latest schema file, it returns the current schema version.
324	func (s *Store) getSchemaVersionOfMigrateScript(filePath string) (string, error) {
325		// If the file is the latest schema file, return the current schema version.
326		if strings.HasSuffix(filePath, LatestSchemaFileName) {
327			return s.GetCurrentSchemaVersion()
328		}
329	
330		normalizedPath := filepath.ToSlash(filePath)
331		elements := strings.Split(normalizedPath, "/")
332		if len(elements) < 2 {
333			return "", errors.Errorf("invalid file path: %s", filePath)
334		}
335		minorVersion := elements[len(elements)-2]
336		rawPatchVersion := strings.Split(elements[len(elements)-1], MigrateFileNameSplit)[0]
337		patchVersion, err := strconv.Atoi(rawPatchVersion)
338		if err != nil {
339			return "", errors.Wrapf(err, "failed to convert patch version to int: %s", rawPatchVersion)
340		}
341		return fmt.Sprintf("%s.%d", minorVersion, patchVersion+1), nil
342	}

52			}

62			}

202	func (s *Store) deleteAttachmentStorageImpl(ctx context.Context, attachment *Attachment, instanceStorageSetting *storepb.InstanceStorageSetting) error {
203		if attachment == nil {
204			return nil
205		}
206		if shouldFailDeleteAttachmentStorage(ctx) {
207			return ErrDeleteAttachmentStorageFailpoint
208		}
209	
210		if attachment.StorageType == storepb.AttachmentStorageType_LOCAL {
211			if err := func() error {
212				p := filepath.FromSlash(attachment.Reference)
213				if !filepath.IsAbs(p) {
214					p = filepath.Join(s.profile.Data, p)
215				}
216				err := os.Remove(p)
217				if err != nil && !os.IsNotExist(err) {
218					return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to delete local file")
219				}
220				return nil
221			}(); err != nil {
222				return err
223			}
224		} else if attachment.StorageType == storepb.AttachmentStorageType_S3 {
225			if err := func() error {
226				s3ObjectPayload := attachment.Payload.GetS3Object()
227				if s3ObjectPayload == nil {
228					return errors.Errorf("No s3 object found")
229				}
230				s3Config := s3ObjectPayload.S3Config
231				if s3Config == nil {
232					if instanceStorageSetting == nil {
233						var err error
234						instanceStorageSetting, err = s.GetInstanceStorageSetting(ctx)
235						if err != nil {
236							return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to get instance storage setting")
237						}
238					}
239					if instanceStorageSetting.S3Config == nil {
240						return errors.Errorf("S3 config is not found")
241					}
242					s3Config = instanceStorageSetting.S3Config
243				}
244	
245				s3Client, err := s3.NewClient(ctx, s3Config)
246				if err != nil {
247					return errors.Wrap(err, "Failed to create s3 client")
248				}
249				if err := s3Client.DeleteObject(ctx, s3ObjectPayload.Key); err != nil {
250					return errors.Wrap(err, "Failed to delete s3 object")
251				}
252				return nil
253			}(); err != nil {
254				return err
255			}
256		}
257	
258		s.deleteAttachmentDerivedCaches(attachment)
259		return nil
260	}

	}

		return nil, status.Errorf(codes.PermissionDenied, "permission denied")
	}

		ContentID: &request.Name,
	})
	if err != nil {
		return nil, status.Errorf(codes.Internal, "failed to list reactions")
	}

	attachments, err := s.Store.ListAttachments(ctx, &store.FindAttachment{

	}

	}

		}
	}

		return nil, status.Errorf(codes.Internal, "failed to delete memo")
	}

		Type:       SSEEventMemoDeleted,
		Name:       request.Name,
		Visibility: memo.Visibility,
		CreatorID:  resolveSSECreatorID(memo, nil),
	})

	return &emptypb.Empty{}, nil
}

202	func (s *Store) deleteAttachmentStorageImpl(ctx context.Context, attachment *Attachment, instanceStorageSetting *storepb.InstanceStorageSetting) error {
203		if attachment == nil {
204			return nil
205		}
206		if shouldFailDeleteAttachmentStorage(ctx) {
207			return ErrDeleteAttachmentStorageFailpoint
208		}
209	
210		if attachment.StorageType == storepb.AttachmentStorageType_LOCAL {
211			if err := func() error {
212				p := filepath.FromSlash(attachment.Reference)
213				if !filepath.IsAbs(p) {
214					p = filepath.Join(s.profile.Data, p)
215				}
216				err := os.Remove(p)
217				if err != nil && !os.IsNotExist(err) {
218					return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to delete local file")
219				}
220				return nil
221			}(); err != nil {
222				return err
223			}
224		} else if attachment.StorageType == storepb.AttachmentStorageType_S3 {
225			if err := func() error {
226				s3ObjectPayload := attachment.Payload.GetS3Object()
227				if s3ObjectPayload == nil {
228					return errors.Errorf("No s3 object found")
229				}
230				s3Config := s3ObjectPayload.S3Config
231				if s3Config == nil {
232					if instanceStorageSetting == nil {
233						var err error
234						instanceStorageSetting, err = s.GetInstanceStorageSetting(ctx)
235						if err != nil {
236							return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to get instance storage setting")
237						}
238					}
239					if instanceStorageSetting.S3Config == nil {
240						return errors.Errorf("S3 config is not found")
241					}
242					s3Config = instanceStorageSetting.S3Config
243				}
244	
245				s3Client, err := s3.NewClient(ctx, s3Config)
246				if err != nil {
247					return errors.Wrap(err, "Failed to create s3 client")
248				}
249				if err := s3Client.DeleteObject(ctx, s3ObjectPayload.Key); err != nil {
250					return errors.Wrap(err, "Failed to delete s3 object")
251				}
252				return nil
253			}(); err != nil {
254				return err
255			}
256		}
257	
258		s.deleteAttachmentDerivedCaches(attachment)
259		return nil
260	}

	memoUID, err := ExtractMemoUIDFromName(request.Name)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, status.Errorf(codes.InvalidArgument, "invalid memo name: %v", err)
	}
	memo, err := s.Store.GetMemo(ctx, &store.FindMemo{
		UID: &memoUID,
	})
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if memo == nil {
		return nil, status.Errorf(codes.NotFound, "memo not found")
	}

	user, err := s.fetchCurrentUser(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, status.Errorf(codes.Internal, "failed to get current user")
	}
	if user == nil {
		return nil, status.Errorf(codes.Unauthenticated, "user not authenticated")
	}
	// Only the creator or admin can update the memo.
	if memo.CreatorID != user.ID && !isSuperUser(user) {
		return nil, status.Errorf(codes.PermissionDenied, "permission denied")
	}

	reactions, err := s.Store.ListReactions(ctx, &store.FindReaction{
		ContentID: &request.Name,
	})
	if err != nil {
		return nil, status.Errorf(codes.Internal, "failed to list reactions")
	}

	attachments, err := s.Store.ListAttachments(ctx, &store.FindAttachment{
		MemoID: &memo.ID,
	})
	if err != nil {
		return nil, status.Errorf(codes.Internal, "failed to list attachments")
	}

	deleteRelations, _ := s.loadMemoRelations(ctx, memo)
	if memoMessage, err := s.convertMemoFromStore(ctx, memo, reactions, attachments, deleteRelations); err == nil {
		// Try to dispatch webhook when memo is deleted.
		if err := s.DispatchMemoDeletedWebhook(ctx, memoMessage); err != nil {
			slog.Warn("Failed to dispatch memo deleted webhook", slog.Any("err", err))
		}
	}

	// Delete memo comments first (store.DeleteMemo handles their relations and attachments)
	commentType := store.MemoRelationComment
	relations, err := s.Store.ListMemoRelations(ctx, &store.FindMemoRelation{RelatedMemoID: &memo.ID, Type: &commentType})
	if err != nil {
		return nil, status.Errorf(codes.Internal, "failed to list memo comments")
	}
	for _, relation := range relations {
		if err := s.Store.DeleteMemo(ctx, &store.DeleteMemo{ID: relation.MemoID}); err != nil {
			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.Internal, "failed to delete memo comment")
		}
	}

	// Delete the memo (store.DeleteMemo handles relation and attachment cleanup)
	if err = s.Store.DeleteMemo(ctx, &store.DeleteMemo{ID: memo.ID}); err != nil {
		return nil, status.Errorf(codes.Internal, "failed to delete memo")
	}

	// Broadcast live refresh event.
	s.SSEHub.Broadcast(&SSEEvent{
		Type:       SSEEventMemoDeleted,
		Name:       request.Name,
		Visibility: memo.Visibility,
		CreatorID:  resolveSSECreatorID(memo, nil),
	})

	return &emptypb.Empty{}, nil
}

13	// ConnectServiceHandler wraps APIV1Service to implement Connect handler interfaces.
14	// It adapts the existing gRPC service implementations to work with Connect's
15	// request/response wrapper types.
16	//
17	// This wrapper pattern allows us to:
18	// - Reuse existing gRPC service implementations
19	// - Support both native gRPC and Connect protocols
20	// - Maintain a single source of truth for business logic.
21	type ConnectServiceHandler struct {
22		*APIV1Service
23	}

25	// NewConnectServiceHandler creates a new Connect service handler.

27		return &ConnectServiceHandler{APIV1Service: svc}

30	// RegisterConnectHandlers registers all Connect service handlers on the given mux.
31	func (s *ConnectServiceHandler) RegisterConnectHandlers(mux *http.ServeMux, opts ...connect.HandlerOption) {
32		// Register all service handlers
33		handlers := []struct {
34			path    string
35			handler http.Handler
36		}{
37			wrap(apiv1connect.NewInstanceServiceHandler(s, opts...)),
38			wrap(apiv1connect.NewAuthServiceHandler(s, opts...)),
39			wrap(apiv1connect.NewUserServiceHandler(s, opts...)),
40			wrap(apiv1connect.NewMemoServiceHandler(s, opts...)),
41			wrap(apiv1connect.NewAttachmentServiceHandler(s, opts...)),
42			wrap(apiv1connect.NewAIServiceHandler(s, opts...)),
43			wrap(apiv1connect.NewShortcutServiceHandler(s, opts...)),
44			wrap(apiv1connect.NewIdentityProviderServiceHandler(s, opts...)),
45		}
46	
47		for _, h := range handlers {
48			mux.Handle(h.path, h.handler)
49		}
50	}

52	// wrap converts (path, handler) return value to a struct for cleaner iteration.
53	func wrap(path string, handler http.Handler) struct {
54		path    string
55		handler http.Handler
56	} {
57		return struct {
58			path    string
59			handler http.Handler
60		}{path, handler}

63	// convertGRPCError converts gRPC status errors to Connect errors.
64	// This preserves the error code semantics between the two protocols.
65	func convertGRPCError(err error) error {
66		if err == nil {
67			return nil
68		}
69		if st, ok := status.FromError(err); ok {
70			return connect.NewError(grpcCodeToConnectCode(st.Code()), err)
71		}
72		return connect.NewError(connect.CodeInternal, err)
73	}

75	// grpcCodeToConnectCode converts gRPC status codes to Connect error codes.
76	// gRPC and Connect use the same error code semantics, so this is a direct cast.
77	// See: https://connectrpc.com/docs/protocol/#error-codes
78	func grpcCodeToConnectCode(code codes.Code) connect.Code {
79		return connect.Code(code)

73				// The RPC method name is set by grpc-gateway after routing. When it can't be

80					if err := authorizer.CheckAccess(ctx, rpcMethod, result); err != nil {
81						http.Error(w, `{"code": 16, "message": "authentication required"}`, http.StatusUnauthorized)

87				if result != nil {

13	// ConnectServiceHandler wraps APIV1Service to implement Connect handler interfaces.
14	// It adapts the existing gRPC service implementations to work with Connect's
15	// request/response wrapper types.
16	//
17	// This wrapper pattern allows us to:
18	// - Reuse existing gRPC service implementations
19	// - Support both native gRPC and Connect protocols
20	// - Maintain a single source of truth for business logic.
21	type ConnectServiceHandler struct {
22		*APIV1Service
23	}
24	
25	// NewConnectServiceHandler creates a new Connect service handler.
26	func NewConnectServiceHandler(svc *APIV1Service) *ConnectServiceHandler {
27		return &ConnectServiceHandler{APIV1Service: svc}
28	}

30	// RegisterConnectHandlers registers all Connect service handlers on the given mux.
31	func (s *ConnectServiceHandler) RegisterConnectHandlers(mux *http.ServeMux, opts ...connect.HandlerOption) {
32		// Register all service handlers
33		handlers := []struct {
34			path    string
35			handler http.Handler
36		}{
37			wrap(apiv1connect.NewInstanceServiceHandler(s, opts...)),
38			wrap(apiv1connect.NewAuthServiceHandler(s, opts...)),
39			wrap(apiv1connect.NewUserServiceHandler(s, opts...)),
40			wrap(apiv1connect.NewMemoServiceHandler(s, opts...)),
41			wrap(apiv1connect.NewAttachmentServiceHandler(s, opts...)),
42			wrap(apiv1connect.NewAIServiceHandler(s, opts...)),
43			wrap(apiv1connect.NewShortcutServiceHandler(s, opts...)),
44			wrap(apiv1connect.NewIdentityProviderServiceHandler(s, opts...)),
45		}
46	
47		for _, h := range handlers {
48			mux.Handle(h.path, h.handler)
49		}
50	}

52	// wrap converts (path, handler) return value to a struct for cleaner iteration.
53	func wrap(path string, handler http.Handler) struct {
54		path    string
55		handler http.Handler
56	} {
57		return struct {
58			path    string
59			handler http.Handler
60		}{path, handler}

63	// convertGRPCError converts gRPC status errors to Connect errors.
64	// This preserves the error code semantics between the two protocols.
65	func convertGRPCError(err error) error {
66		if err == nil {
67			return nil
68		}
69		if st, ok := status.FromError(err); ok {
70			return connect.NewError(grpcCodeToConnectCode(st.Code()), err)
71		}
72		return connect.NewError(connect.CodeInternal, err)
73	}

75	// grpcCodeToConnectCode converts gRPC status codes to Connect error codes.
76	// gRPC and Connect use the same error code semantics, so this is a direct cast.
77	// See: https://connectrpc.com/docs/protocol/#error-codes
78	func grpcCodeToConnectCode(code codes.Code) connect.Code {
79		return connect.Code(code)

11	// SSEEventType represents the type of change event.

23	// SSEEvent represents a change event sent to SSE clients.
24	type SSEEvent struct {
25		Type SSEEventType `json:"type"`
26		// Name is the affected resource name (e.g., "memos/xxxx").
27		// For reaction events, this is the memo resource name that the reaction belongs to.
28		Name string `json:"name"`

36	// JSON returns the JSON representation of the event.

38	func (e *SSEEvent) JSON() []byte {
39		data, err := json.Marshal(e)
40		if err != nil {
41			slog.Error("failed to marshal SSE event", "err", err, "event", e)
42			return nil
43		}
44		return data

47	// SSEClient represents a single SSE connection.
48	type SSEClient struct {
49		events chan []byte
50		userID int32
51		role   store.Role
52	}

54	// SSEHub manages SSE client connections and broadcasts events.
55	// It is safe for concurrent use.
56	type SSEHub struct {
57		mu      sync.RWMutex
58		clients map[*SSEClient]struct{}
59		closed  bool
60	}
61	
62	// NewSSEHub creates a new SSE hub.
63	func NewSSEHub() *SSEHub {
64		return &SSEHub{
65			clients: make(map[*SSEClient]struct{}),
66		}
67	}
68	
69	// Subscribe registers a new client and returns it.
70	// The caller must call Unsubscribe when done.
71	func (h *SSEHub) Subscribe(userID int32, role store.Role) *SSEClient {
72		c := &SSEClient{
73			// Buffer a few events so a slow client doesn't block broadcasting.
74			events: make(chan []byte, 32),
75			userID: userID,
76			role:   role,
77		}
78		h.mu.Lock()
79		if h.closed {
80			close(c.events)
81		} else {
82			h.clients[c] = struct{}{}
83		}
84		h.mu.Unlock()
85		return c
86	}
87	
88	// Unsubscribe removes a client and closes its channel.
89	func (h *SSEHub) Unsubscribe(c *SSEClient) {
90		h.mu.Lock()
91		if _, ok := h.clients[c]; ok {
92			delete(h.clients, c)
93			close(c.events)
94		}
95		h.mu.Unlock()
96	}
97	
98	// Close disconnects all subscribed SSE clients.
99	func (h *SSEHub) Close() {
100		h.mu.Lock()
101		defer h.mu.Unlock()
102		if h.closed {
103			return
104		}
105		h.closed = true
106		for c := range h.clients {
107			delete(h.clients, c)
108			close(c.events)
109		}
110	}

112	// Broadcast sends an event to all connected clients.
113	// Slow clients that have a full buffer will have the event dropped
114	// to avoid blocking the broadcaster.
115	func (h *SSEHub) Broadcast(event *SSEEvent) {
116		data := event.JSON()
117		if len(data) == 0 {
118			return
119		}
120		h.mu.RLock()
121		defer h.mu.RUnlock()
122		for c := range h.clients {
123			if !c.canReceive(event) {
124				continue
125			}
126			select {
127			case c.events <- data:
128			default:
129				// Drop event for slow client to avoid blocking.
130			}
131		}
132	}

49		w.Header().Set("Cache-Control", "no-cache")
50		w.Header().Set("Connection", "keep-alive")
51		w.Header().Set("X-Accel-Buffering", "no") // Disable nginx buffering

55		if f, ok := w.(http.Flusher); ok {

59		// Subscribe to the hub.
60		client := hub.Subscribe(userID, role)

64		heartbeat := time.NewTicker(sseHeartbeatInterval)

71		// Send an initial comment so clients and dev proxies observe the stream
72		// immediately instead of waiting for the first heartbeat or data event.
73		if _, err := fmt.Fprint(w, ": connected\n\n"); err != nil {

75		}
76		if f, ok := w.(http.Flusher); ok {
77			f.Flush()
78		}
79	
80		for {
81			select {
82			case <-ctx.Done():
83				// Client disconnected.
84				slog.Debug("SSE client disconnected", "userID", userID)
85				return nil
86	
87			case data, ok := <-client.events:

93				if _, err := fmt.Fprintf(w, "data: %s\n\n", data); err != nil {

102				if _, err := fmt.Fprint(w, ": heartbeat\n\n"); err != nil {
103					return nil
104				}
105				if f, ok := w.(http.Flusher); ok {

69	// Subscribe registers a new client and returns it.
70	// The caller must call Unsubscribe when done.
71	func (h *SSEHub) Subscribe(userID int32, role store.Role) *SSEClient {
72		c := &SSEClient{
73			// Buffer a few events so a slow client doesn't block broadcasting.
74			events: make(chan []byte, 32),
75			userID: userID,
76			role:   role,
77		}
78		h.mu.Lock()
79		if h.closed {
80			close(c.events)
81		} else {
82			h.clients[c] = struct{}{}
83		}
84		h.mu.Unlock()
85		return c

88	// Unsubscribe removes a client and closes its channel.

90		h.mu.Lock()

92			delete(h.clients, c)

94		}

98	// Close disconnects all subscribed SSE clients.

34	func handleSSE(c *echo.Context, hub *SSEHub, authenticator *auth.Authenticator) error {
35		// Authenticate the request.
36		authHeader := c.Request().Header.Get("Authorization")

78		}

## Live Event Broadcasting Mechanism Report

### Mechanism: Server-Sent Events (SSE)

The project uses **Server-Sent Events (SSE)** for live event broadcasting to browsers. The implementation allows browsers to maintain a persistent HTTP connection to receive real-time events about memo changes, comments, and reactions.

### SSE Hub Implementation File

**Location:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/sse_hub.go`

**Key Components:**
- **SSEHub struct** - Manages all SSE client connections with thread-safe broadcasting
- **SSEClient struct** - Represents individual SSE connections with a buffered channel (32-event buffer)
- **Core Methods:**
  - `NewSSEHub()` - Creates a new hub
  - `Subscribe(userID, role)` - Registers a client connection
  - `Unsubscribe(client)` - Disconnects a client
  - `Broadcast(event)` - Sends an event to all connected clients
  - `Close()` - Gracefully shuts down all connections

**Supporting Files:**
- `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/sse_handler.go` - HTTP handler that manages SSE connections
- `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/sse_event_helpers.go` - Helper functions for building SSE events

### Memo Handler Methods That Broadcast Events

The following handler methods in the APIV1Service call `SSEHub.Broadcast()` to notify connected clients:

1. **`CreateMemo()`** (memo_service.go)
   - Broadcasts: `SSEEventMemoCreated` event
   - Condition: Only broadcasts if SSE is not suppressed (skipped when called internally from CreateMemoComment)

2. **`DeleteMemo()`** (memo_service.go)
   - Broadcasts: `SSEEventMemoDeleted` event

3. **`CreateMemoComment()`** (memo_service_comments.go)
   - Broadcasts: `SSEEventMemoCommentCreated` event
   - Notifies about new comments on parent memos

4. **`dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects()`** (memo_update_helpers.go)
   - Broadcasts: `SSEEventMemoUpdated` event
   - Handles memo update side effects and notifications

5. **`UpsertMemoReaction()`** (reaction_service.go)
   - Broadcasts: `SSEEventReactionUpserted` event
   - Uses helper function `buildMemoReactionSSEEvent()`

6. **`DeleteMemoReaction()`** (reaction_service.go)
   - Broadcasts: `SSEEventReactionDeleted` event
   - Uses helper function `buildMemoReactionSSEEvent()`

### Supported Event Types

- `memo.created` - When a memo is created
- `memo.updated` - When a memo is modified
- `memo.deleted` - When a memo is deleted
- `memo.comment.created` - When a comment is added to a memo
- `reaction.upserted` - When a reaction is added/modified
- `reaction.deleted` - When a reaction is removed

Events include visibility metadata (`Visibility` and `CreatorID`) that the hub uses to filter delivery:
- **Private events**: Only delivered to the creator or admins
- **Public/Protected events**: Delivered to all connected clients

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. - update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". 11	// SSEEventType represents the type of change event.
12	type SSEEventType string
13	
14	const (
15		SSEEventMemoCreated        SSEEventType = "memo.created"
16		SSEEventMemoUpdated        SSEEventType = "memo.updated"
17		SSEEventMemoDeleted        SSEEventType = "memo.deleted"
18		SSEEventMemoCommentCreated SSEEventType = "memo.comment.created"
19		SSEEventReactionUpserted   SSEEventType = "reaction.upserted"
20		SSEEventReactionDeleted    SSEEventType = "reaction.deleted"
21	)
22	
23	// SSEEvent represents a change event sent to SSE clients.
24	type SSEEvent struct {
25		Type SSEEventType `json:"type"`
26		// Name is the affected resource name (e.g., "memos/xxxx").
27		// For reaction events, this is the memo resource name that the reaction belongs to.
28		Name string `json:"name"`
29		// Parent is the parent memo resource name when the affected resource is a comment.
30		Parent string `json:"parent,omitempty"`
31		// Visibility and CreatorID are used only for server-side delivery filtering.
32		Visibility store.Visibility `json:"-"`
33		CreatorID  int32            `json:"-"`
34	}
35	
36	// JSON returns the JSON representation of the event.
37	// Returns nil if marshaling fails (error is logged).
38	func (e *SSEEvent) JSON() []byte {
39		data, err := json.Marshal(e)
40		if err != nil {
41			slog.Error("failed to marshal SSE event", "err", err, "event", e)
42			return nil
43		}
44		return data
45	}
46	
47	// SSEClient represents a single SSE connection.
48	type SSEClient struct {
49		events chan []byte
50		userID int32
51		role   store.Role
52	}
53	
54	// SSEHub manages SSE client connections and broadcasts events.
55	// It is safe for concurrent use.
56	type SSEHub struct {
57		mu      sync.RWMutex
58		clients map[*SSEClient]struct{}
59		closed  bool
60	}
61	
62	// NewSSEHub creates a new SSE hub.
63	func NewSSEHub() *SSEHub {
64		return &SSEHub{
65			clients: make(map[*SSEClient]struct{}),
66		}
67	}
68	
69	// Subscribe registers a new client and returns it.
70	// The caller must call Unsubscribe when done.
71	func (h *SSEHub) Subscribe(userID int32, role store.Role) *SSEClient {
72		c := &SSEClient{
73			// Buffer a few events so a slow client doesn't block broadcasting.
74			events: make(chan []byte, 32),
75			userID: userID,
76			role:   role,
77		}
78		h.mu.Lock()
79		if h.closed {
80			close(c.events)
81		} else {
82			h.clients[c] = struct{}{}
83		}
84		h.mu.Unlock()
85		return c
86	}
87	
88	// Unsubscribe removes a client and closes its channel.
89	func (h *SSEHub) Unsubscribe(c *SSEClient) {
90		h.mu.Lock()
91		if _, ok := h.clients[c]; ok {
92			delete(h.clients, c)
93			close(c.events)
94		}
95		h.mu.Unlock()
96	}
97	
98	// Close disconnects all subscribed SSE clients.
99	func (h *SSEHub) Close() {
100		h.mu.Lock()
101		defer h.mu.Unlock()
102		if h.closed {
103			return
104		}
105		h.closed = true
106		for c := range h.clients {
107			delete(h.clients, c)
108			close(c.events)
109		}
110	}
111	
112	// Broadcast sends an event to all connected clients.
113	// Slow clients that have a full buffer will have the event dropped
114	// to avoid blocking the broadcaster.
115	func (h *SSEHub) Broadcast(event *SSEEvent) {
116		data := event.JSON()
117		if len(data) == 0 {
118			return
119		}
120		h.mu.RLock()
121		defer h.mu.RUnlock()
122		for c := range h.clients {
123			if !c.canReceive(event) {
124				continue
125			}
126			select {
127			case c.events <- data:
128			default:
129				// Drop event for slow client to avoid blocking.
130			}
131		}
132	}

134	func (c *SSEClient) canReceive(event *SSEEvent) bool {
135		switch event.Visibility {
136		case store.Private:
137			return c.userID == event.CreatorID || c.role == store.RoleAdmin
138		case store.Public, store.Protected, "":
139			return true
140		default:
141			slog.Warn("SSE canReceive: unknown visibility type, denying event", "visibility", event.Visibility)
142			return false
143		}

15	const (
16		// sseHeartbeatInterval is the interval between heartbeat pings to keep the connection alive.
17		sseHeartbeatInterval = 30 * time.Second
18	)
19	
20	type sseRouteRegistrar interface {
21		GET(path string, h echo.HandlerFunc, m ...echo.MiddlewareFunc) echo.RouteInfo
22	}
23	
24	// RegisterSSERoutes registers the SSE endpoint on the given Echo router.
25	func RegisterSSERoutes(router sseRouteRegistrar, hub *SSEHub, storeInstance *store.Store, secret string) {
26		authenticator := auth.NewAuthenticator(storeInstance, secret)
27		router.GET("/api/v1/sse", func(c *echo.Context) error {
28			return handleSSE(c, hub, authenticator)
29		})
30	}

32	// handleSSE handles the SSE connection for live memo refresh.
33	// Authentication is done via Bearer token in the Authorization header.
34	func handleSSE(c *echo.Context, hub *SSEHub, authenticator *auth.Authenticator) error {
35		// Authenticate the request.
36		authHeader := c.Request().Header.Get("Authorization")
37		result := authenticator.Authenticate(c.Request().Context(), authHeader)
38		if result == nil {
39			return c.JSON(http.StatusUnauthorized, map[string]string{"error": "authentication required"})
40		}
41		userID, role := getSSEClientIdentity(result)
42		if userID == 0 {
43			return c.JSON(http.StatusUnauthorized, map[string]string{"error": "authentication required"})
44		}
45	
46		// Set SSE headers.
47		w := c.Response()
48		w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "text/event-stream")
49		w.Header().Set("Cache-Control", "no-cache")
50		w.Header().Set("Connection", "keep-alive")
51		w.Header().Set("X-Accel-Buffering", "no") // Disable nginx buffering
52		w.WriteHeader(http.StatusOK)
53	
54		// Flush headers immediately.
55		if f, ok := w.(http.Flusher); ok {
56			f.Flush()
57		}
58	
59		// Subscribe to the hub.
60		client := hub.Subscribe(userID, role)
61		defer hub.Unsubscribe(client)
62	
63		// Create a ticker for heartbeat pings.
64		heartbeat := time.NewTicker(sseHeartbeatInterval)
65		defer heartbeat.Stop()
66	
67		ctx := c.Request().Context()
68	
69		slog.Debug("SSE client connected", "userID", userID)
70	
71		// Send an initial comment so clients and dev proxies observe the stream
72		// immediately instead of waiting for the first heartbeat or data event.
73		if _, err := fmt.Fprint(w, ": connected\n\n"); err != nil {
74			return nil
75		}
76		if f, ok := w.(http.Flusher); ok {
77			f.Flush()
78		}
79	
80		for {
81			select {
82			case <-ctx.Done():
83				// Client disconnected.
84				slog.Debug("SSE client disconnected", "userID", userID)
85				return nil
86	
87			case data, ok := <-client.events:
88				if !ok {
89					// Channel closed, client was unsubscribed.
90					return nil
91				}
92				// Write SSE event.
93				if _, err := fmt.Fprintf(w, "data: %s\n\n", data); err != nil {
94					return nil
95				}
96				if f, ok := w.(http.Flusher); ok {
97					f.Flush()
98				}
99	
100			case <-heartbeat.C:
101				// Send a heartbeat comment to keep the connection alive.
102				if _, err := fmt.Fprint(w, ": heartbeat\n\n"); err != nil {
103					return nil
104				}
105				if f, ok := w.(http.Flusher); ok {
106					f.Flush()
107				}
108			}
109		}
110	}

## Live Event Broadcasting Mechanism Report

### Mechanism: Server-Sent Events (SSE)

The project uses **Server-Sent Events (SSE)** for live event broadcasting to browsers. The implementation allows browsers to maintain a persistent HTTP connection to receive real-time events about memo changes, comments, and reactions.

### SSE Hub Implementation File

**Location:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/sse_hub.go`

- **SSEHub struct** - Manages all SSE client connections with thread-safe broadcasting
- **SSEClient struct** - Represents individual SSE connections with a buffered channel (32-event buffer)

66	    return (changed ? { ...data, pages } : data) as T;

202	      const memo = await memoServiceClient.updateMemo({

208	    onMutate: async ({ update }) => {
209	      if (!update.name) {
210	        return { previousMemo: undefined };
211	      }
212	
213	      // Cancel outgoing refetches to prevent race conditions
214	      await queryClient.cancelQueries({ queryKey: memoKeys.all });
215	
216	      // Snapshot previous value for rollback on error
217	      const previousMemo =
218	        queryClient.getQueryData<Memo>(memoKeys.detail(update.name)) || findMemoInCollectionQueries(queryClient, update.name);

227	      return { previousMemo };
228	    },
229	    onError: (_err, { update }, context) => {
230	      // Rollback on error
231	      if (context?.previousMemo && update.name) {
232	        queryClient.setQueryData(memoKeys.detail(update.name), context.previousMemo);
233	        patchMemoInCollectionQueries(queryClient, context.previousMemo);
234	      } else {
235	        queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: memoKeys.all });
236	      }
237	    },
238	    onSuccess: (updatedMemo) => {
239	      // Update cache with server response
240	      queryClient.setQueryData(memoKeys.detail(updatedMemo.name), updatedMemo);
241	      patchMemoInCollectionQueries(queryClient, updatedMemo);

244	      if (updatedMemo.parent) {
245	        queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: memoKeys.comments(updatedMemo.parent) });

249	    },

13	// Engine parses CEL filters into a dialect-agnostic condition tree.
14	type Engine struct {
15		schema Schema
16		env    *cel.Env
17		// nowFunc resolves the value of the `now` variable. It is frozen once per
18		// Compile so a single filter sees a single instant, and is overridable in
19		// tests for deterministic folding.
20		nowFunc func() time.Time
21	}

23	// NewEngine builds a new Engine for the provided schema.
24	func NewEngine(schema Schema) (*Engine, error) {
25		env, err := cel.NewEnv(schema.EnvOptions...)
26		if err != nil {
27			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to create CEL environment")
28		}
29		return &Engine{
30			schema:  schema,
31			env:     env,
32			nowFunc: time.Now,
33		}, nil
34	}

47	// Compile parses the filter string into an executable program.
48	func (e *Engine) Compile(_ context.Context, filter string) (*Program, error) {
49		if strings.TrimSpace(filter) == "" {
50			return nil, errors.New("filter expression is empty")
51		}
52	
53		ast, issues := e.env.Compile(filter)
54		if issues != nil && issues.Err() != nil {
55			return nil, errors.Wrap(issues.Err(), "failed to compile filter")
56		}
57		parsed, err := cel.AstToParsedExpr(ast)
58		if err != nil {
59			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to convert AST")
60		}
61	
62		cond, err := buildCondition(parsed.GetExpr(), parseContext{schema: e.schema, now: e.nowFunc()})
63		if err != nil {
64			return nil, err
65		}
66	
67		return &Program{
68			schema:    e.schema,
69			condition: cond,
70		}, nil
71	}

74	func (e *Engine) CompileToStatement(ctx context.Context, filter string, opts RenderOptions) (Statement, error) {
75		program, err := e.Compile(ctx, filter)

2	
3	This package houses the memo-only filter engine that turns standard CEL syntax
4	into SQL fragments for the subset of expressions supported by the memo schema.
5	The engine follows a three phase pipeline inspired by systems
6	such as Calcite or Prisma:
7	
8	1. **Parsing** – CEL expressions are parsed with `cel-go` and validated against
9	   the memo-specific environment declared in `schema.go`. Only fields that
10	   exist in the schema can surface in the filter, and non-standard legacy
11	   coercions are rejected.
12	2. **Normalization** – the raw CEL AST is converted into an intermediate
13	   representation (IR) defined in `ir.go`. The IR is a dialect-agnostic tree of
14	   conditions (logical operators, comparisons, list membership, etc.). This
15	   step enforces schema rules (e.g. operator compatibility, type checks).
16	3. **Rendering** – the renderer in `render.go` walks the IR and produces a SQL
17	   fragment plus placeholder arguments tailored to a target dialect
18	   (`sqlite`, `mysql`, or `postgres`). Dialect differences such as JSON access,
19	   boolean semantics, placeholders, and `LIKE` vs `ILIKE` are encapsulated in
20	   renderer helpers.
21	
22	The entry point is `filter.DefaultEngine()` from `engine.go`. It lazily constructs
23	an `Engine` configured with the memo schema and exposes:
24	
25	```go
26	engine, _ := filter.DefaultEngine()
27	stmt, _ := engine.CompileToStatement(ctx, `has_task_list && visibility == "PUBLIC"`, filter.RenderOptions{
28		Dialect: filter.DialectPostgres,
29	})
30	// stmt.SQL  -> "((memo.payload->'property'->>'hasTaskList')::boolean IS TRUE AND memo.visibility = $1)"
31	// stmt.Args -> ["PUBLIC"]
32	```
33	
34	## Core Files
35	
36	| File          | Responsibility                                                                  |
37	| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
38	| `schema.go`   | Declares memo fields, their types, backing columns, CEL environment options     |
39	| `ir.go`       | IR node definitions used across the pipeline                                    |
40	| `parser.go`   | Converts CEL `Expr` into IR while applying schema validation                    |
41	| `render.go`   | Translates IR into SQL, handling dialect-specific behavior                      |
42	| `engine.go`   | Glue between the phases; exposes `Compile`, `CompileToStatement`, and `DefaultEngine` |
43	| `helpers.go`  | Convenience helpers for store integration (appending conditions)                |
44	
45	## SQL Generation Notes
46	
47	- **Placeholders** — `?` is used for SQLite/MySQL, `$n` for Postgres. The renderer
48	  tracks offsets to compose queries with pre-existing arguments.
49	- **JSON Fields** — Memo metadata lives in `memo.payload`. The renderer handles
50	  `JSON_EXTRACT`/`json_extract`/`->`/`->>` variations and boolean coercion.
51	- **Time Fields** — `created_ts`, `updated_ts`, and attachment `create_time` are
52	  CEL `timestamp` values. Express instants with the `now` variable,
53	  `duration("…")` (e.g. `created_ts >= now - duration("24h")`), or
54	  `timestamp("2006-01-02T15:04:05Z")` / `timestamp(<epoch-seconds>)`. These fold
55	  to epoch seconds at compile time — `now` is frozen once per compile (injectable
56	  for tests via the engine clock) — so the backing columns stay unchanged.
57	- **Tag Operations** — `tag in [...]` and `"tag" in tags` become JSON array
58	  predicates. SQLite uses `LIKE` patterns, MySQL uses `JSON_CONTAINS`, and
59	  Postgres uses `@>`.
60	- **Boolean Flags** — Fields such as `has_task_list` render as `IS TRUE` equality
61	  checks, or comparisons against `CAST('true' AS JSON)` depending on the dialect.
62	- **String Matching** — `content.contains(x)`, `content.startsWith(x)`, and
63	  `content.endsWith(x)` render as case-insensitive `LIKE`/`ILIKE` with LIKE
64	  metacharacters (`%`, `_`, `\`) escaped. Available on scalar string fields whose
65	  schema sets `SupportsContains` (memo `content`; attachment `filename`,
66	  `mime_type`).
67	- **Regex** — `field.matches("pattern")` renders to `~` (Postgres) or `REGEXP`
68	  (MySQL/SQLite). SQLite uses a Go-backed `regexp` function registered in
69	  `store/db/sqlite/functions.go`. Patterns are validated at compile time against
70	  Go's RE2 via `cel.ValidateRegexLiterals()`. **Caveat:** regex *syntax* differs
71	  per engine (Go RE2 on SQLite, POSIX ERE on Postgres, ICU on MySQL 8.0+), so
72	  engine-specific patterns may not be portable.
73	- **Tag `all()` / `exists_one()`** — `tags.all(t, <pred>)` matches only non-empty
74	  tag sets where every element satisfies the predicate; `tags.exists_one(t,
75	  <pred>)` matches when exactly one element does (`COUNT(...) = 1`). Both iterate
76	  per-element (`json_each` / `jsonb_array_elements_text` / `JSON_TABLE`).
77	- **Timestamp Accessors** — `created_ts.getFullYear()`, `getMonth()`, `getDate()`,
78	  `getDayOfMonth()`, `getDayOfWeek()`, `getDayOfYear()`, `getHours()`,
79	  `getMinutes()`, `getSeconds()` render to date-part extraction (`strftime` /
80	  `EXTRACT` / `YEAR`/`MONTH`/…). Results are normalized to CEL's base (0-based
81	  month, 0-based day-of-week with 0 = Sunday). The same accessors on `now` fold
82	  to literal date parts of the frozen evaluation time (UTC), so saved filters
83	  like `created_ts.getMonth() == now.getMonth() && created_ts.getDate() ==
84	  now.getDate()` ("on this day") re-resolve on every compile. Extraction is UTC
85	  on SQLite/Postgres (epoch columns); on MySQL the `TIMESTAMP` column is read in
86	  the session time zone. A timezone argument is not supported.
87	- **Set Operations** — `ext.Sets()`: `sets.contains(tags, [...])`,
88	  `sets.intersects(tags, [...])`, and `sets.equivalent(tags, [...])` desugar to
89	  exact-membership checks (AND / OR of `"v" in tags`); `equivalent` adds a
90	  `size(tags)` length check (relies on tags being a set).
91	- **`size()`** — `size(tags)` renders to JSON array length; `size(content)` (and
92	  other string fields) render to `LENGTH` / `CHAR_LENGTH` (MySQL) for code-point
93	  counts.
94	- **Arithmetic** — `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`, `%` constant-fold on literal/`now`/`duration`
95	  operands (division and modulo guard against a zero divisor).
96	
97	## Typical Integration
98	
99	1. Fetch the engine with `filter.DefaultEngine()`.
100	2. Call `CompileToStatement` using the appropriate dialect enum.
101	3. Append the emitted SQL fragment/args to the existing `WHERE` clause.
102	4. Execute the resulting query through the store driver.
103	
104	The `helpers.AppendConditions` helper encapsulates steps 2–3 when a driver needs
105	to process an array of filters.

2	
3	import (
4		"fmt"
5		"strings"
6	
7		"github.com/pkg/errors"
8	)
9	
10	type renderer struct {
11		schema             Schema
12		dialect            DialectName
13		placeholderOffset  int
14		placeholderCounter int
15		args               []any
16	}
17	
18	type renderResult struct {
19		sql           string
20		trivial       bool
21		unsatisfiable bool
22	}
23	
24	func newRenderer(schema Schema, opts RenderOptions) *renderer {
25		return &renderer{
26			schema:            schema,
27			dialect:           opts.Dialect,
28			placeholderOffset: opts.PlaceholderOffset,
29		}
30	}
31	
32	func (r *renderer) Render(cond Condition) (Statement, error) {
33		result, err := r.renderCondition(cond)
34		if err != nil {
35			return Statement{}, err
36		}
37		args := r.args
38		if args == nil {
39			args = []any{}
40		}
41	
42		switch {
43		case result.unsatisfiable:
44			return Statement{
45				SQL:  "1 = 0",
46				Args: args,
47			}, nil
48		case result.trivial:
49			return Statement{
50				SQL:  "",
51				Args: args,
52			}, nil
53		default:
54			return Statement{
55				SQL:  result.sql,
56				Args: args,
57			}, nil
58		}
59	}
60	
61	func (r *renderer) renderCondition(cond Condition) (renderResult, error) {
62		switch c := cond.(type) {
63		case *LogicalCondition:
64			return r.renderLogicalCondition(c)
65		case *NotCondition:
66			return r.renderNotCondition(c)
67		case *FieldPredicateCondition:
68			return r.renderFieldPredicate(c)
69		case *ComparisonCondition:
70			return r.renderComparison(c)
71		case *InCondition:
72			return r.renderInCondition(c)
73		case *ElementInCondition:
74			return r.renderElementInCondition(c)
75		case *TextMatchCondition:
76			return r.renderTextMatch(c)
77		case *RegexCondition:
78			return r.renderRegex(c)
79		case *ListComprehensionCondition:
80			return r.renderListComprehension(c)
81		case *ConstantCondition:
82			if c.Value {
83				return renderResult{trivial: true}, nil
84			}
85			return renderResult{sql: "1 = 0", unsatisfiable: true}, nil
86		default:
87			return renderResult{}, errors.Errorf("unsupported condition type %T", c)
88		}
89	}
90	
91	func (r *renderer) renderLogicalCondition(cond *LogicalCondition) (renderResult, error) {
92		left, err := r.renderCondition(cond.Left)
93		if err != nil {
94			return renderResult{}, err
95		}
96		right, err := r.renderCondition(cond.Right)
97		if err != nil {
98			return renderResult{}, err

39	func (s *APIV1Service) checkMemoReadAccess(ctx context.Context, memo *store.Memo) error {
40		if memo == nil {
41			return status.Errorf(codes.NotFound, "memo not found")
42		}
43	
44		// Archived memos are only visible to their creator.
45		if memo.RowStatus == store.Archived {
46			user, err := s.fetchCurrentUser(ctx)
47			if err != nil {
48				return status.Errorf(codes.Internal, "failed to get user")
49			}
50			if user == nil || memo.CreatorID != user.ID {
51				return status.Errorf(codes.NotFound, "memo not found")
52			}
53		}
54	
55		if memo.Visibility != store.Public {
56			user, err := s.fetchCurrentUser(ctx)
57			if err != nil {
58				return status.Errorf(codes.Internal, "failed to get user")
59			}
60			if user == nil {
61				return status.Errorf(codes.Unauthenticated, "user not authenticated")
62			}
63			if memo.Visibility == store.Private && memo.CreatorID != user.ID {
64				return status.Errorf(codes.PermissionDenied, "permission denied")
65			}
66		}
67		return nil
68	}
